title: [05/03/2023] - Waste paper recycling process
prompt: The chart below shows the process of waste paper recycling. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the process by which waste paper is recycled to produce usable paper products.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the waste paper recycling process consists of six main stages, beginning with the collection of waste paper and culminating in the production of new paper through machine manufacturing. This represents a cyclical process that transforms discarded paper materials into reusable products.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The process commences with the collection of waste paper from two primary sources: public paper banks and businesses. Following collection, the waste paper undergoes sorting by hand, during which paper is graded according to quality and unsuitable materials are removed. The sorted paper is then transported to paper mills for further processing.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Upon arrival at the paper mill, the waste paper enters the cleaning stage, where it undergoes cleaning, pulping, and the removal of other materials such as staples. Subsequently, the paper moves to the de-inking phase, during which inks and glues are eliminated from the pulped material. Finally, the cleaned and de-inked pulp is fed into paper making machines, which manufacture usable paper products, thereby completing the recycling cycle.
